title: Transport for NSW launches the PAWS AI animal-detection and smart-signage trial on the Monaro Highway between Bredbo and Williamsdale; no outcome yet
summary: Transport for NSW's Protective Animal Warning System: two AI-enabled roadside cameras on a 13 km Monaro Highway stretch trigger driver warnings; trial announced 18 July 2026, no results yet.
account: The NSW Government announced its Protective Animal Warning System trial on July 18, 2026. Transport for NSW developed the system, which uses thermal and optical cameras with AI to recognize wildlife and trigger roadside warnings. The announcement describes training at Yennora and Symbio Wildlife Park before a live trial on the Monaro Highway. About Regional’s separate interviews add the planned two-camera layout on a 13 km stretch between Bredbo and Williamsdale and the role of local wildlife carers. The intended benefit is fewer collisions after drivers receive warnings. Neither source reports a measured change in detection accuracy, driver behavior, or collisions.
purpose: Detect wildlife near the road and warn drivers dynamically to limit wildlife-vehicle strikes; no benefit has yet been observed.
system: PAWS (Protective Animal Warning System): heat-sensing and optical roadside cameras with a species-trained AI model triggering warning signs
location: Monaro Highway between Bredbo and Williamsdale, New South Wales, Australia
domain: Road safety and wildlife-vehicle collision prevention
